comment: Guest contract revisions (ANTC_REVISION) and the first Antinomie version that shipped each. A revision changes only with a minor or major release (x.y.0); bases record the matching version as min_app_version. Bases from before revision 9 carry no revision.

revisions.notes: 0.9.0 adds the debug breakpoint kind BP_HW_READ (5, load-only watchpoints) without a new revision: it is offered only through the revision-20 CAPS flag READ_WATCH (arm64 guests), so an older host never sends it and an older or x86-64 guest never offers it.

Task-exit records name the sender of the signal that ended a task (lifecycle.signal.*) and carry the kernel's OOM kill line (lifecycle.kernel_log); the recorder decodes the ioctl requests fs/ioctl.c answers for every file and arch_prctl ARCH_CET_STATUS. arm64 guests write ELF32 cores of AArch32 tasks (core flag COMPAT_ELF32 0x100, CORE_CAPS 32) and debug them (debug CAPS AARCH32 4096; A32 and Thumb software breakpoints); a debug-on-start session of an image the engine cannot debug answers EOPNOTSUPP. ioctl arguments are captured by their encoded size and more by layout (ifreq, ifconf, loop_info64, loop_config, file_clone_range, fsxattr); reads of event descriptors name their records; common compat calls are captured by ILP32 layouts.

A specimen acquisition can carry the SHA-256 of the copy the guest keeps (EXEC flag SPECIMEN_DIGEST 64, ACQUIRE header flag DIGEST 1, offered in TRACER_CAPS): the host copy of an uploaded program is vouched for at the launch reply, even when the program exits within milliseconds, and a launch the guest refused gets static analysis of the file it was asked to run. A run with a core on suspicious activity holds each process at its exit for at most 50 ms until the host has judged it (EXEC flag EXIT_HOLD 128, command EXIT_HOLD 0x1068, record lifecycle.exit_hold, core flag EXIT_HELD 0x200), so a process that exits a millisecond after its match still gets its core. Each feature is asked for only where the guest offers it, so a revision-21 base runs on this host without them.
